plan_a_advantages: More diverse session types (intervals, tempo, varied long runs) cater to a broader range of speed development needs.
Includes dedicated hill sessions alongside other workouts, providing a more complete hill training experience.
Long runs are varied in duration and intensity, simulating different race distances and terrain.
plan_b_advantages: Focuses heavily on climbing strength, which is a valuable attribute for trail running.
Shorter overall duration, potentially reducing the risk of overtraining for a runner who isn't already highly experienced.
reasoning: Plan A is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster. It incorporates a wider variety of session types – long runs, intervals, tempo runs, and hill sessions – which directly addresses the multifaceted demands of trail running. Plan B, while including hill work, heavily emphasizes climbing strength with repetitive threshold hill sessions, potentially leading to overtraining and neglecting other crucial aspects of trail speed development like sustained aerobic capacity and race-pace running. Plan A’s inclusion of tempo runs and varied long run durations provides a more balanced approach to building both endurance and speed.
